state.input: Build an internal tool for our support team. Staff paste a customer's issue and the tool drafts a reply using our knowledge base, with an audit trail of what was sent. Around 50 support agents will use it daily. We need role-based access (agents vs admins), full history of every reply, and a dashboard showing response times. Our stack is Next.js and Postgres.

suitability.reason: The workflow lacks a critical integration step. It treats the knowledge base as an abstract task without defining how the data is ingested, cleaned, or kept in sync with the source of truth, which is essential for an AI-driven support tool. Furthermore, it assumes the AI drafting logic can be built in isolation from the UI, but the user experience (streaming responses, editing drafts) is highly dependent on the API design.
suitability.suggestedWorkflow: 1. Define Knowledge Base Source: Identify the source of truth (e.g., Notion, Zendesk, or Markdown files) and establish an ingestion pipeline to sync data into a vector database. 2. Database & Auth Setup: Design the Postgres schema and implement NextAuth with RBAC to secure the application. 3. AI Pipeline Development: Build the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) backend, including document chunking, vector search, and LLM integration. 4. Core API Development: Create endpoints for draft generation, ensuring the logic handles the context window and prompt engineering effectively. 5. Frontend Development: Build the agent interface, focusing on the input form, draft display, and the 'send/edit' workflow. 6. Audit & Logging: Implement the logging service to capture every interaction, including timestamps for response time calculation. 7. Admin Dashboard: Build the visualization layer for metrics. 8. Testing & Deployment: Perform user acceptance testing with a small group of agents and deploy to production.
suitability.suggestedSummary: The workflow is updated to prioritize data ingestion from the knowledge base and integrate the AI pipeline more tightly with the frontend interaction requirements.

flaws.title: Missing Secrets Management
flaws.description: The plan does not mention how API keys for the language model or database credentials will be stored securely.
flaws.suggestedFix: Implement a secrets management solution like Vercel Environment Variables or AWS Secrets Manager to store sensitive keys.

flaws.title: Lack of Rate Limiting
flaws.description: The tool is vulnerable to abuse or accidental cost spikes if an agent or malicious actor triggers the LLM API repeatedly.
flaws.suggestedFix: Implement rate limiting on the API endpoints using Upstash Redis or similar to prevent excessive API calls.

flaws.title: Missing Data Privacy and PII Handling
flaws.description: The plan does not address PII (Personally Identifiable Information) redaction before sending customer data to an external LLM.
flaws.suggestedFix: Add a preprocessing step to scrub PII from customer issues before sending them to the LLM API.

flaws.title: Absence of Error Handling and Fallback Logic
flaws.description: The workflow assumes the LLM will always return a valid response, ignoring potential API timeouts or model failures.
flaws.suggestedFix: Implement robust error handling and a fallback mechanism (e.g., a generic template response) if the LLM service is unavailable.

flaws.title: No Logging or Observability Strategy
flaws.description: While an audit trail is mentioned, there is no mention of system-level logging for debugging errors or tracking performance issues.
flaws.suggestedFix: Integrate a logging service like Sentry or Logtail to monitor application errors and performance metrics.

flawReport.summary: The plan covers the functional requirements well but lacks critical security infrastructure (secrets management, rate limiting, PII protection) and operational robustness (error handling, system logging). These gaps pose risks to data privacy and service reliability.

executions.output:
```prisma
// prisma/schema.prisma
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Prisma schema for the Support Ticket Drafting Tool
// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

/**
 * Roles for role‑based access control
 */
model Role {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  name        String   @unique
  description String?

  users User[]

  @@map("roles")
}

/**
 * Users of the system
 */
model User {
  id            Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  email         String   @unique
  name          String?
  passwordHash  String?   // if using local auth
  roleId        Int
  role          Role     @relation(fields: [roleId], references: [id])

  ticketsAssigned Ticket[] @relation("AssignedTickets")
  ticketsCreated  Ticket[] @relation("CreatedTickets")
  responses       Response[]
  drafts          TicketResponseDraft[]

  @@map("users")
}

/**
 * Support tickets
 */
model Ticket {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  description String
  status      TicketStatus @default(PENDING)
  priority    TicketPriority @default(MEDIUM)

  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  createdById Int
  createdBy   User @relation("CreatedTickets", fields: [createdById], references: [id])

  assignedToId Int?
  assignedTo   User? @relation("AssignedTickets", fields: [assignedToId], references: [id])

  responses   Response[]
  drafts      TicketResponseDraft[]

  @@map("tickets")
}

/**
 * Responses to tickets (finalised replies)
 */
model Response {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  content   String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  ticketId Int
  ticket   Ticket @relation(fields: [ticketId], references: [id])

  authorId Int
  author   User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])

  @@map("responses")
}

/**
 * Drafts of ticket responses (editable by agents)
 */
model TicketResponseDraft {
  id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  content   String
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt

  ticketId Int
  ticket   Ticket @relation(fields: [ticketId], references: [id])

  authorId Int
  author   User @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])

  @@map("ticket_response_drafts")
}

/**
 * Knowledge base articles
 */
model KnowledgeBaseArticle {
  id          Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  title       String
  content     String
  tags        String[] @default([]) // simple array of tags
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt

  @@map("knowledge_base_articles")
}

/**
 * Enumerations for ticket status and priority
 */
enum TicketStatus {
  PENDING
  IN_PROGRESS
  RESOLVED
  CLOSED
}

enum TicketPriority {
  LOW
  MEDIUM
  HIGH
  CRITICAL
}
```

**Setup Notes**

1. **Install Prisma**  
   ```bash
   npm install @prisma/client prisma
   npx prisma init
   ```

2. **Configure `.env`**  
   ```env
   DATABASE_URL="postgresql://USER:PASSWORD@HOST:PORT/DATABASE?schema=public"
   ```

3. **Generate Client**  
   ```bash
   npx prisma generate
   ```

4. **Create Migration**  
   ```bash
   npx prisma migrate dev --name init
   ```

5. **Use in Next.js API Routes**  
   ```ts
   import { PrismaClient } from '@prisma/client';
   const prisma = new PrismaClient();
   ```

This schema provides a relational foundation for role‑based access, ticket lifecycle, response drafting, and knowledge‑base integration, all managed through Prisma ORM.
